title: chromolaena squalida
intro: Chromolaena squalida, commonly known as Mexican mint marigold or Wild Marigold, is a plant species in the sunflower family, Asteraceae. It has been used in traditional medicine for various health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties, which may help to reduce pain, fever, and inflammation. The bioactive constituents present in Chromolaena squalida include terpenoids, flavonoids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its therapeutic actions, such as its ability to modulate the immune system and exhibit antiviral and antiparasitic activities. Additionally, the plant's leaves and flowers have been used to treat various health conditions, including respiratory issues, digestive problems, and skin infections.
